title: Cloud shelf packaging checklist and copyboard
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working copy for packaging Redwood Inference products for cloud marketplaces (AWS, GCP, Azure) and partner storefronts. It combines a technical/operational listing checklist with short/long copy variants and buyer-focused messaging that product, partner ops, and legal can iterate on. Use this as the single working board for the first wave of marketplace launches (hosted API + dedicated + private).

Scope and intended outcomes:
- Define required artifacts for each marketplace (metadata, binaries/container images, SaaS entitlement configs, licensing text).
- Provide concise copy variants for 1-line, 40–60 word, and 250–400 word descriptions targeted at Platform Engineers, ML Engineers, and Procurement.
- Map pricing/commitment models to marketplace billing constructs (metered SaaS, paid AMI/VM, subscription).
- Create a go/no-go checklist covering security, legal, observability, and support readiness.
- Surface open questions and owners for final sign-off.

Target marketplaces & constraints (quick notes):
- AWS Marketplace (SaaS and AMI): supports metered SaaS billing but requires AWS Seller registration, security review, and specific entitlements/config files. AMI/EC2 delivery option needs hardened AMI build and marketplace product listing ID.
- GCP Marketplace: supports container and VM images + SaaS. Has image vulnerability policies; requires Cloud Partner Advantage enrollment for some features.
- Azure Marketplace: supports managed apps and VM images; procurement/customer legal flow expects Microsoft NCE compatibility for some enterprise buys.
- Partner storefronts (ISV partner portals): variable metadata required; often need co-brand guidelines and approved logo assets.

Packaging checklist (technical + assets) — baseline for each marketplace (finals can vary by target):
- Product metadata file (JSON/YAML) with: shortName, longName, category tags, keywords, regions, support contact, documentation URL, TOS/Privacy link.
- Short tagline (<= 10 words).
- 40–60 word summary (for catalog tiles).
- 250–400 word description (detailed feature and value bullets).
- 3–5 screenshots: console onboarding, dashboard, latency/cost dashboard, rollout control. Provide PNGs at recommended sizes.
- 1 architecture diagram (SVG + PNG) showing: customer app -> Redwood API endpoint -> model variants -> caches -> optional private deployment path. Include text alt.
- Deployment artifacts (choose per marketplace):
  - AWS SaaS: SaaS entitlement integration manifest, API endpoints, SSO/OAuth guidance if applicable, usage reporting hooks, CloudFormation examples (if needed).
  - AWS AMI/EC2: hardened AMI ID, startup scripts, pre-bundled model weights location (if allowed), security hardening checklist.
  - GCP container: OCI image URI, Helm chart (optional), deployment README, service account scopes required.
  - Azure VM/Managed App: image or ARM template, required role assignments, storage/account requirements.
- Entitlement & billing mapping: SKU names, unit-of-measure (token/embedding-embed-unit/concurrent-rps), pricing tiers mapping.
- Test account & test buyer flow to validate purchase-to-provision lifecycle.
- Security artifacts: SOC2 summary (or link), penetration test date/report, data processing agreement (DPA) snippet for marketplace consumption, list of supported KMS providers.
- Logs/observability examples: screenshots or sample traces showing per-route latency breakdowns.
- Support & SLA text: support contact, response times by severity, scheduled maintenance policy, uptime SLA (if offered).
- Legal: approved marketplace T&Cs excerpt, export controls statement, open-source component inventory (SBOM) as required.

Copyboard: short variants (testing lines)
- Tagline options (pick 1):
  - "Predictable LLM inference, everywhere."
  - "Low-latency LLM inference for production apps."
  - "Serve LLMs at scale—secure, fast, cost-aware."

- 40–60 word catalog tile options:
  - Platform Engineer: "Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime to serve large language models with predictable latency and cost. Choose hosted, dedicated, or private deployments, with built-in caching, batching, and fallbacks to keep critical services online. Includes observability and rollout controls for safe production launches."
  - ML Engineer: "Optimize inference for quality and cost: Redwood's runtime picks kernels, manages KV caches, and suggests quantization policies per workload. Ship safer model rollouts with built-in eval hooks, canary deployments, and per-route latency insights."
  - Procurement-focused: "Turnkey inference with enterprise SLAs: reserved capacity options, private deployments, and billing models that map to usage or committed capacity. Backed by compliance artifacts and flexible support tiers."

Full description (250–400 words) — unified base version (editable):
"Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform that makes serving large language models predictable and economical. Our high-throughput runtime optimizes kernels, batching, and KV caching to reduce per-token cost while meeting strict latency SLOs. Choose hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and isolation, or Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) for regulated environments.

The platform includes first-class observability and operational tooling: per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, model rollouts (canary and A/B), and automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants under capacity stress. Integration points include a straightforward REST/SDK interface, built-in streaming and function calling, and options for enterprise key management (KMS/HSM) and audit logs.

Redwood helps teams ship LLM features faster while controlling production economics: intelligent batching, cache suggestions, and quantization recommendations tailored to your workload. We support common compliance needs and provide enterprise SLAs and professional services for private or on-prem deployments."

Persona-targeted bullets (for body/feature list):
- For Platform/Infra: predictable throughput, autoscaling policies, reserved capacity, and routing controls by region/cost/latency.
- For ML Eng: quantization and model variant recommendations, eval hooks, and request-level tracing for quality regressions.
- For Product: streaming responses, function/tool calling, structured output support, and built-in monitoring for cost/latency.

Pricing & SKU mapping guidance (working rules):
- Hosted SaaS (marketplace-metered): map to per-1k-token units or per-embedding unit. Create SKU names like RI-HOST-TOKEN-1K and RI-HOST-EMB-1.
- Dedicated (reserved): SKU maps to monthly committed GPU-equivalent hours or vCPU+RAM buckets. Provide clear overage rates.
- Private (license): one-time platform fee + support/maintenance recurring SKU.
- For marketplaces that don't support metered billing: offer subscription tiers with token caps and overage thresholds.

Security & compliance sign-off checklist (pre-launch):
- SOC2 Type II summary available and linked.
- DPA template uploaded and referenced in listing.
- SBOM attached (OS + 3rd-party libs) and licenses reviewed.
- Pen test report dated within 12 months attached.
- KMS integrations documented and tested for private deployments.
- Data residency wording approved for regions we sell into.

Operational readiness (launch checklist):
- Buyer provisioning flow tested end-to-end (purchase -> entitlement -> provisioning).
- Onboarding email templates drafted and approved.
- Support runbook for marketplace buys prepared (including how to escalate to SRE and AM).
- Observability templates (default dashboards, alerting thresholds) included in docs.
- Billing reconciliation test completed for at least one sandbox purchase.

Open questions / decisions needed (owners):
- Final SKU names & unit definitions (Owner: Liam O'Connor) — JIRA GT-6123.
- Which deployment artifacts to include in first launch (SaaS + container only?) (Owner: Mei Chen).
- Legal signoff on marketplace T&Cs and export control language (Owner: Diego Alvarez).
- Support SLA levels for marketplace purchases vs direct enterprise contracts (Owner: Arjun Mehta).

Launch timeline (high-level):
- Week 0–2: finalize SKU mapping, create product metadata files, gather compliance artifacts.
- Week 3: build marketplace-specific artifacts (manifests, images, screenshots), internal test purchases.
- Week 4: security/legal review and final corrections.
- Week 5: submit for marketplace review (sla depending on marketplace).

Action items (short):
- Priya: consolidate final screenshots and architecture SVG (due 2025-11-10).
- Liam: lock SKU names and publish to GT-6123 (due 2025-11-07).
- Mei: assemble container image + deployment README for GCP + Azure (due 2025-11-17).
- Diego: initial legal review of marketplace T&Cs (due 2025-11-12).

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally a mix of copy + tactical checklist — use the copy sections as A/B test variants for catalog tiles and the checklist as an operational playbook.
- If marketplace-specific rules contradict items here, defer to the marketplace policy doc linked in linked_artifacts.

End working board — leave comments inline in this doc and add any market-specific items under the marketplace name (e.g., "AWS SaaS notes") as separate sections.

Draft history / provenance: created as a consolidation of the go-to-market scrum brainstorm (2025-10-01) and the partner ops meeting (2025-10-22).
